# Results -- Study 112 (Move-Index) on real daily tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The ICE BofA MOVE index
(``^MOVE``) as a cross-asset equity risk gauge: does high or rising MOVE predict
negative forward SPY returns, and does MOVE add anything over VIX?  Daily data
``^MOVE``, ``^VIX``, SPY from Yahoo Finance.  As-of **2026-06-13**.*

## Data stamp

| Ticker | Window | n obs | Fingerprint |
|---|---|--:|---|
| ^MOVE | 2003-01-06 to 2026-06-12 | 5,796 | `74dbe2ac989f` |
| ^VIX  | 2003-01-06 to 2026-06-12 | 5,796 | (same cache) |
| SPY   | 2003-01-06 to 2026-06-12 | 5,796 | (same cache) |

MOVE range: 36.6 – 264.6 (mean 86.8, std 30.5). VIX range: 9.1 – 82.7 (mean 19.1, std 8.4).
MOVE-VIX correlation: 0.586 — they co-move in stress episodes but are not interchangeable.

## Test 1 — MOVE quintile vs forward SPY returns

Days sorted into MOVE quintiles by rolling 252-day percentile rank (strict out-of-sample).
Forward log-return from close of day *t* to close of day *t+h*.

| Horizon | Q5 (high MOVE) | Q1 (low MOVE) | Q5-Q1 spread (bps) | HAC *t*-spread |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1 day   | +4.1 bps | +4.8 bps | **-0.7 bps** | **-0.76** |
| 5 days  | +22.7 bps | +22.6 bps | **+0.1 bps** | **-0.68** |
| 21 days | +68.7 bps | +96.8 bps | **-28.1 bps** | **-1.63** |

At every horizon the Q5-Q1 spread is statistically indistinguishable from zero (|*t*| < 2 in all
cases). If anything, high-MOVE days see *slightly* lower forward returns at the 21-day horizon
(t = −1.63), but this is not significant at conventional levels and could easily be a chance finding
given the overlap in 21-day forward windows.

## Test 2 -- MOVE vs VIX incremental regression

OLS of forward SPY return on standardised MOVE and VIX (both z-scored rolling OOS, directly comparable):

| Horizon | n | beta_MOVE | t_MOVE | beta_VIX | t_VIX | R² |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1 day  | 5,733 | -0.00009 | **-0.80** | +0.00019 | +1.02 | 0.00031 |
| 5 days | 5,729 | -0.00029 | **-0.59** | +0.00020 | +0.23 | 0.00018 |
| 21 days| 5,713 | -0.00122 | **-0.95** | +0.00096 | +0.49 | 0.00093 |

Neither MOVE nor VIX is a significant predictor of forward SPY returns at any horizon. MOVE's
t-stat is well below 2 across all horizons. VIX is also not significant. The regression R² is
essentially zero (< 0.001), confirming that both bond-vol and equity-vol indices are coincident risk
gauges, not forward-looking equity predictors.

## Test 3 -- MOVE/VIX ratio signal

The MOVE/VIX ratio captures relative stress (bond vol vs equity vol). High ratio = bond markets more
stressed than equity markets, potentially a cross-asset warning signal.

| Horizon | n | beta_ratio | t_ratio | Q5-Q1 spread (bps) | t_spread |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1 day   | 5,733 | -0.00016 | **-1.23** | -1.8 bps | -0.35 |
| 5 days  | 5,729 | -0.00057 | **-1.02** | -11.8 bps | -0.53 |
| 21 days | 5,713 | -0.00236 | **-1.65** | -54.6 bps | -0.93 |

The ratio is directionally consistent (negative beta: high MOVE/VIX predicts slightly worse
returns) but never reaches significance (|*t*| < 2 everywhere). The signal is NONE.

## Synthetic positive control

On a deterministic synthetic tape with tunable `move_signal`, the quintile spread grows
monotonically and becomes significant (|*t*| > 2) at `move_signal >= 0.01`. On the null tape
(`move_signal = 0`) the spread is ~0. This confirms the engine is a faithful detector — the
real tape simply has no exploitable MOVE signal to harvest.

## Verdict

- **Signal -- NONE.** MOVE quintile spread is -0.7 bps at h=1d (HAC *t* = -0.76), +0.1 bps at
  h=5d (t = -0.68), -28.1 bps at h=21d (t = -1.63). No horizon clears the |*t*| >= 2 bar. MOVE
  adds nothing over VIX (t_MOVE = -0.80 in joint regression). The MOVE/VIX ratio also fails
  (t_ratio = -1.02 to -1.65 across horizons).
- **Tradability -- MIRAGE.** With no measurable signal, there is no trading strategy to evaluate.
  Even if the 21-day effect were real, a daily-rebalanced factor built on monthly-horizon signals
  would carry enormous turnover costs and overnight gap risk.
- **Beats VIX? -- NO.** MOVE and VIX are correlated (0.59) but neither adds incremental
  information over the other in forecasting forward SPY returns at any tested horizon.
